items.title: Tom Varner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 13, 2025
items.q: There’s a fantastic alto player named Mark Taylor in Seattle who had studied with Dick Oatts, the great sax player

ctx.x: Yeah. That music had very specific – we all had parts. So I would go [scats] and then the trumpet [scats]. That was very written out. And then the changes I gave to the alto sax. He had nothing written to actually play though. He just soloed over the whole thing. Like, kind of like Lee Konitz might, or, he had studied, there’s a guy named Mark Taylor but

not the French horn player Mark Taylor. There’s lots of Mark Taylors. There’s a fantastic alto player named Mark Taylor in Seattle who had studied with Dick Oatts, the great sax player, and he had some of that approach in there too. But he did have a set of changes but only a set of changes for that particular piece. There were other tracks on that that were just little meditations. And then the other ones were much more big, thick, massive like Messiaen crazy chords, very fat parallel motion of like everybody…
Speaking of that, parallel notes, “Choppy and Dumb”?
